stage_a.note: Founder greets with a bright smile, enthusiastic voice, and positive energy from the start.
Founder uses animated, expansive gestures to emphasize the staggering amount of single-use plastics.
Founder bows to the panel, smiling warmly, demonstrating a highly approachable and friendly demeanor.

venture.description: Edible, mass-manufacturable cutlery designed to replace single-use plastic utensils.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh introduces himself and Incredible Eats, pitching edible cutlery as a solution to single-use plastic waste.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara handles the product and asks what they are eating.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark jokes that he doesn't care and is going to eat a spork.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel asks how long it takes for the cutlery to decompose.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh answers by stating how long the spoons stay firm in hot soup and ice cream.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara remarks that the product tastes very good.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks how many calories are in a chopstick.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh states that a chopstick is about 15 calories.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori praises the taste of the spicy pizza-flavored spoon, saying she would buy them as snacks.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh points out the vanilla-flavored spoon in the ice cream, explaining it tastes like a waffle cone.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori picks up an item and asks what it is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh clarifies that the item Lori holds is a straw.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks what flavor the straw is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh answers that the straw is actually flavorless.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if Dinesh is concerned about the flavor of the utensils in addition to their functionality.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh explains they keep flavors subtle for food service so as not to overpower the food being eaten.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara asks what it costs to make the spoon and what it sells for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh states the spoon sells for 20 cents and costs 10 cents to make.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks for the cost differential between large volume plastic spoons and the edible spoon.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh notes plastic spoons cost 1 to 2 cents, but explains how businesses can upsell edible spoons for additional profit.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin presses on what the cost difference is for a business that does not want to upsell.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh explains they have brought the price down from 35 cents to 20 cents and aim for 15 cents.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara remarks that the price still seems pricey.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel asks if Dinesh has sold any product yet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh states he has sold 1.2 million spoons over the past two and a half years.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks what that volume translates to in dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh replies that sales total about $170,000.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks where the spoons are currently being sold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh explains they started in B2B food service but expanded to B2C and direct-to-consumer due to COVID-19.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin questions how consumers will know it is edible without heavy education, challenging the cost premium for businesses.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori steps in to counter Kevin, suggesting the spoons could easily have 'eat me' imprinted on them.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin challenges back, arguing that paying 20 times more is still a barrier regardless of an imprint.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara remarks on Dinesh's visible excitement, inviting him to share more about his feelings.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh explains it is his dream to be there as an immigrant, having found his life's purpose in reducing plastic waste.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin attempts to steer the conversation back to the financial aspects of the business.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori interrupts Kevin, stating she wants to hear more about Dinesh's personal background.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asserts that while the mission is wonderful, his main concern is making money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh promises they will learn a bit more about him.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori jokingly tells the room to quit focusing on Kevin.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh addresses Kevin, acknowledging money but recounting his journey from India and his desire to change the planet.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara tells Dinesh that while his enthusiasm is great, he seems blinded by it regarding the business realities.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara explains that raising costs for restaurants is too challenging and not practical enough, so she drops out.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel disagrees with Barbara about passion, but notes a large gap between Dinesh's vision and investor expectations.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel states he cannot justify the $7.1 million valuation based on $170,000 in sales, so he exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh defends the valuation, arguing he has spent nothing on marketing and has built a viral-capable product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel reassures Dinesh that he thinks he will succeed, despite not investing at that valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh politely thanks the investors who have exited for their time.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin calls the idea brilliant but the valuation absurd, offering the requested $500,000 for a 35% stake.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh thanks Kevin for making the offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark comments to Kevin that he thinks Kevin's vision for the product is too small.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark praises the product as a game changer, suggesting it could be sold individually as an upsell everywhere.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark offers $500,000 for 20% equity, citing the amount of time he would need to invest.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin interjects that he prefers his own offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori announces that she also has an offer for Dinesh.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori states that both previous offers miss the bigger picture, believing the product can succeed in all markets.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori argues she is the right shark to help blitz the market.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori makes an offer of $500,000 for a 15% stake in the company.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin recaps the three standing offers from Mark, himself, and Lori, asking Dinesh what he wants to do.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel declares he is coming back into the negotiation because he finds Dinesh so compelling.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daniel makes an offer of $500,000 for 25% equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh asks the panel if he is allowed to make a counter-offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh asks if any of the sharks would accept 12% equity for the $500,000.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori explicitly declines Dinesh's counter-offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark withdraws his offer, stating that Dinesh's preset limit shows he does not truly value the investors.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin reminds Dinesh that he still has active offers to consider.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori points out that her offer is the closest to what he asked for, wondering why he hesitates.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dinesh accepts Lori's offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori celebrates the deal and goes to hug Dinesh.

decisions.note: Believes raising costs for restaurants from 1 cent to 20 cents is too challenging and impractical.
Cannot justify the $7.1 million valuation based on only $170,000 in lifetime sales.
Likes the idea but thinks the valuation is absurd.
Believes the product is a game changer but will require a lot of his time.
Believes she is the right shark to help him blitz the market across all channels.

decisions.terms: I'm going to come back in.
decisions.note: Finds the founder delightfully compelling and wants to participate.
Offers his help to grow the business.
Asks if any of the sharks would accept a 12% stake.
Feels the founder's preset limit shows he doesn't truly value the investors' contributions.
Accepts Lori's 15% offer after she points out it is the closest to his counter.

record.notes: The founder's counter-offer was directed at the panel generally, but since Lori had the 15% offer, it is coded as countering O3.
